title: Lo the Destroying Angel Flies
description: Lo the Destroying Angel Flies in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 155, headed “Christ our passover”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Lo the de-stroy-ing an-gel flies To Pharao-h's stub-born land: The pride and flower of E-gypt dies By his vin-dic-tive hand.

lines: The pride and flower of Egypt dies
He pass'd the tents of Jacob o'er,
He saw the blood on every door,
Thus th' appointed Lamb must bleed
Thus Israel is from bondage freed,
Lord, if my heart were sprinkled too
With blood so rich as thine,

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
